formula: Thévenin: U = E − r·I   ⇔   Norton: I = I₀ − U/r  avec  I₀ = E/r
sketch:
Observe: schematic canvas with a real generator (E, r) driving a
variable load R. Two side panels show the Thévenin model (voltage
source E in series with r) and the Norton model (current source I₀
in parallel with conductance G₀ = 1/r). Sliders: E, r, R. Live
readouts of U(R) and I(R) confirm both models yield identical
terminal behavior. Experiment: given a Thévenin source, derive the
equivalent Norton (or vice versa) by choosing I₀, G₀; students
verify equivalence by matching U(R) curves. Evaluate: one model
hidden; student picks the missing parameters. Wrinkle: three-terminal
"black box" mode — student determines (E_eq, r_eq) from two measured
operating points, without ever seeing inside.
